name: pickup-spawn
demonstrates: PickupManager schedules the first pickup spawn ~8s after a run begins (per PickupManagerTests) and each pickup persists for a ~20s lifetime, placed on a street tile clear of adjacent buildings (per the placement-search rules pinned by PickupIntegrationTests). This journey waits ~12s past PLAY (past the 8s first-spawn delay with margin for the placement search and frame timing) and takes a screenshot labelled pickup-spawned, reviewed for a small bobbing med-kit or garbage-can icon rendered over an accent-tinted pad -- the tint sits on the pad only, never on the icon itself -- sitting on a street tile and depth-sorted correctly next to any nearby building (not overlapping or drawn behind it), with med kits and garbage cans visually distinguishable from one another. It then waits a further ~6s (now ~18s past PLAY, inside the pickup's lifetime window and past a plausible player-collection window) and takes a second screenshot labelled pickup-lifecycle, reviewed to confirm the pickup mechanic keeps operating over time (the original pickup still aging/present, replaced, or freshly collected) rather than a one-shot spawn that never recurs. That second wait targets ~18s rather than the ~22s an earlier draft used, because the frozen numbers in PickupKind.tuningTable leave a recurring EMPTY window that a later frame can fall into: cadence (25s) is longer than lifetime (20s) and a kind's cadence re-arms only after a successful spawn, so the effective ceiling is one pickup at a time -- the first pickup expires at ~PLAY+28s and the next one cannot appear before ~PLAY+33s (see the PickupKind.Tuning.maxAlive doc note). navigate is vision-located and each wait starts only after the previous step returns, so ~18s keeps roughly 10s of cumulative slop in hand before that 28-33s dead zone. A reviewer who still lands on an empty street in this frame should read it as that timing artifact rather than as a regression. Camera-independence is explicitly NOT claimed by these screenshots: no step here moves the camera (this journey's action vocabulary is wait / assert_running / screenshot / navigate), so the player stands at the spawn junction for the whole run and the frames cannot distinguish "lifetime is aged by deltaTime only" from "the pickup survived because the camera never moved". That property -- a pickup is never deleted merely because the camera moved -- is pinned by PickupManagerTests.test_largeVisibleRectJumpBetweenUpdates_doesNotAffectPickupAging, which teleports visibleRect a million points between two update calls and asserts expiry still lands on real accumulated deltaTime. Gate is human/vision review of both screenshots; assert_running steps only confirm the app process is still alive. The underlying spawn timing, placement rules, bobbing/tinted rendering, collection and depth-sort behavior are already pinned by PickupManagerTests, PickupNodeTests, PickupIntegrationTests, RaccoonPickupDiversionTests and PlayerHealTests -- this journey exists purely so the runtime probe captures frames late enough for a pickup to actually be on screen, instead of the menu-to-gameplay journey's 5s screenshot which fires well before the first pickup can possibly exist.

steps.target: the large neon-outlined PLAY button in the middle of the title screen that starts a new run (NOT the plain HIGH SCORES button below it)
steps.expect: the running game -- a playable isometric city scene with a ground lattice, buildings and a player actor, not a menu or title screen
